$comment: Authoring input for `npm run sprites:emotions`. Nothing here ships to the browser — it
is the prompt book for the Ludo.ai generator, and the record of what each clip was asked
to be, so a re-run reproduces the same intent.
Prompt rules learned the hard way, keep to them:
- Describe POSTURE, not expression. A Trial sprite's face is 50-80px on screen; a raised
eyebrow is invisible and asking for one just wastes the model's attention.
- Say 'in place', 'no travel'. Left unsaid, the model walks the animal out of frame and
the clip cannot loop against a static stage slot.
- Framing comes from each animal's `view`, never from the prompt text: the cast is NOT
uniformly side-on. The owl is drawn front-facing and the raccoon's sitting pose is a
three-quarter — telling either of them 'side view, facing left' asks the generator to
turn the character, and the clip then will not cut against its own idle loop.
- Keep the silhouette. The reference frame carries the character; the prompt should only
ever move it.
- Never name a posture the animal has to CHANGE STATE to reach. 'Crouched low' made the
generator lie the donkey down over the clip and never stand it back up: a transition,
not a held attitude, and one that cannot loop. Say what the body does while it stays
where it is, and say outright what it must not do ('never lies down').
- Watch the height swing in the review output. The runtime scales a clip off one union
bounding box, so a character whose height wanders 20%+ across frames renders too small
for most of the clip however good it looks in isolation.

$faceComment: Authoring input for `npm run sprites:emotions -- --faces`, which cuts dialogue portraits
out of the promoted BODY clips. It calls no API and spends no credits.
This block used to hold a prompt vocabulary for generating headshots through Ludo. That was
tried three times and abandoned: the eyelid aperture swung 165%, 196% and 458% across the
clip, and two attempts invented teeth the reference does not have. It is not a prompt
problem — the endpoint reframes its input (a head sent at a 485x363 box came back at
257x192), so it redraws the head from scratch in every frame rather than animating the
pixels it was given, and no instruction makes a redrawn eye match the one before it. The
body clips already show the cast talking, and their faces hold still because the generator
was animating posture. See the header of scripts/ludo/cropFace.mjs.
C1. `headCrop` is the crop rect, in fractions of the character's UNION ALPHA BOX across
all frames of its `talking` body clip — not of the cell, and not of the reference
frame the old `face` rect used. Bodies sit at different offsets in their cells, so a
cell-relative number would not transfer; the union box makes it mean 'the leading
half of the silhouette, top 69% down'.
C2. Negative x/y are normal and deliberate: they reach into the transparent margin so an
ear or muzzle is not cropped hard against its own outline. Values past 1.0 are fine
too and get clamped — a front-facing head can be wider than the body box.
C3. ONE RECT PER ANIMAL, never one per emotion, and one alignment template per animal
taken from its `talking` clip. All five portraits play in the same box in the same
dialogue, so a tighter `angry` rect would make the head jump size when the beat
changes speaker emotion.
C4. PART OF THE BODY IN SHOT IS FINE. A portrait is head-and-shoulders: the neck and
chest filling the bottom edge is what makes it read as a portrait rather than a
floating head. Do not tighten the rect to exclude them.
C5. TUNE IT FREE. `--faces --dry-run` writes every crop and a review page and promotes
nothing. Judge each crop at BOTH sizes the page shows: 112px is what ships, 224px is
what a 2x display renders, and softness only shows at the second.
C6. WATCH THE ALIGNMENT NUMBERS, not the height swing. The head bobs through a body clip
(the fox's moves 30px, its `thinking` 40px) and the cropper tracks it frame by frame.
`align` saturating its search window means the crop is being clipped rather than
followed; a large `jump` between consecutive frames means the matcher lost its lock.
The eight gallery-only animals (cow, mouse, pig, brown-bull, white-chicken,
skunk, seagull, snake) have a seeded `headCrop` but no body clips, so a full-cast `--faces`
run skips them without needing a flag. `dog` has both. A seeded rect is a guess: it is
relative to a `talking` clip that does not exist yet, so retune it (free) once one does.

phases.$comment: Pilot phased emotion.
